2026 demonstrated how quickly disruption can reshape global energy markets. Conflict in the Middle East disrupted production and exports, restricted critical trade routes and affected energy infrastructure, with repercussions across oil, gas, LNG and power markets.
For traders, the year highlighted the connections between physical supply, trade flows, inventories, demand and regional market dynamics.
Our latest guide looks back at the defining developments of 2026 and the signals traders needed to follow across global energy markets. Fill in the form to download your copy, or read on to explore what’s covered.
What defined energy trading in 2026?
The guide explores the key questions that emerged across oil, gas, LNG and power markets:

What defined oil trading in 2026? From disruption in the Strait of Hormuz and US$100/bbl Brent to demand destruction and extreme crack-spread volatility.

What defined gas and LNG trading in 2026? From the attacks on Ras Laffan and soaring global gas prices to changing LNG flows and a renewed focus on security of supply.

What defined power trading in 2026? From the global repercussions of the Middle East conflict to changing fuel economics, nuclear policy and renewable supply-chain risks.
